methodological_rigor.justification: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 6 diagnostic studies (lung cancer + bone metastasis detection). Bivariate Reitsma random-effects model appropriate for sensitivity-specificity correlation. Heterogeneity assessment via Cochran's Q and I2; robustness examined through leave-one-out sensitivity analysis (minimal fluctuations: sensitivity 0.832–0.878, specificity 0.854–0.891). PROSPERO registration, PRISMA guidelines followed. QUADAS-2 and NOS for quality assessment. Appropriate statistical methods throughout.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy studies for computer-based image processing (AI, machine learning, radiomics, CNN) in detecting bone metastasis in lung cancer patients. Diagnostic utility (high sensitivity 0.86, specificity 0.88, AUC 0.931) supports clinical implementation. However, LoE 4 (case series aggregated) rather than higher given heterogeneous studies and indirect clinical evidence.

reporting_quality.justification: Systematic review fully adheres to PRISMA guidelines with PROSPERO registration. Comprehensive search across 6 databases (PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane, Web of Science, clinicaltrials.gov) through December 2024. Detailed data extraction, QUADAS-2 and NOS quality assessment, sensitivity analyses. Results presented with forest plots, SROC curves, AUC estimates. Limitations section addresses small number of included studies (n=6) and heterogeneity in imaging modalities/algorithms.

novelty_literature.justification: First meta-analysis specifically focused on computer-based image processing for bone metastasis detection in lung cancer. Builds on prior narrative reviews of AI in diagnosis. Main finding—high sensitivity (0.86) and specificity (0.88) for computer-based techniques—expected given maturation of deep learning methods. Incremental contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized Introduction establishing epidemiology of bone metastasis in lung cancer and clinical need for early diagnosis, detailed Methods with comprehensive search strategy and statistical approach, Results systematically presenting pooled diagnostic metrics with subgroup analyses by imaging modality and algorithm type, Discussion appropriately contextualizing findings. Tables and figures support narrative effectively.

key_strengths: First meta-analysis specifically focused on diagnostic accuracy of computer-based image processing for bone metastasis in lung cancer; fills evidence gap regarding AI clinical utility
High diagnostic accuracy demonstrated: sensitivity 0.86 (95% CI 0.78–0.91), specificity 0.88 (95% CI 0.86–0.90), AUC 0.931; excellent NPV (high reliability for ruling out non-metastatic disease)
Robust methodology: PROSPERO registration, PRISMA adherence, bivariate Reitsma model, QUADAS-2/NOS quality assessment, sensitivity analyses showing minimal fluctuation (robust findings)
Subgroup analyses examining heterogeneity by imaging modality (CT vs SPECT/scintigraphy) and algorithm type (AI/deep learning vs radiomics) providing clinically useful stratification
key_concerns: Limited number of eligible studies (n=6) reduces power; heterogeneity in imaging modalities (CT, SPECT, dual-energy CT), preprocessing methods, and computational algorithms may limit pooled estimates generalizability

Diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis (not randomized trials) subject to verification bias: only patients undergoing imaging AND biopsy included, overestimating true performance in clinical screening scenarios
Publication bias potential acknowledged but not thoroughly assessed (Deeks' test not reported for <10 studies)
Heterogeneous study designs (cross-sectional, diagnostic cohorts) and quality (2 studies with moderate-to-high bias risk retained post-consensus); quality variation may influence pooled estimates
Lack of discussion regarding cost-effectiveness, workflow integration, or comparative head-to-head performance of different computational approaches limiting clinical implementation guidance
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality systematic review and meta-analysis with prospective registration establishing high diagnostic accuracy (AUC 0.931) for computer-based image processing in bone metastasis detection. Robust methodology with sensitivity analyses confirming findings. Suitable for Tier 2 publication; recommend minor revisions discussing clinical implementation barriers and cost-effectiveness considerations alongside diagnostic performance.
